stem: According to Article XIV, Section 7 of the 1987 Constitution, what are the official languages of the Philippines for purposes of communication and instruction?
hints: Do not mix up the national language with the official languages. Article XIV names them in different sections.
Section 6 names the national language. Section 7 names the official languages "For purposes of communication and instruction."

Section 7 lists two official languages, one of them only "until otherwise provided by law." It calls regional languages auxiliary and says Spanish and Arabic are only promoted "on a voluntary and optional basis." Pick the choice that names just the two.

solution.methodName: Find the provision, then match the key words

steps.action: Find the national language: "The national language of the Philippines is Filipino" (Section 6).
steps.why: The national language is the one language of the whole nation.

steps.action: Find the official languages: "the official languages of the Philippines are Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English" (Section 7).
steps.why: Official languages are the ones used for government communication and for teaching in schools. There are two.

steps.action: Place the other languages: regional languages are "the auxiliary official languages in the regions," and "Spanish and Arabic shall be promoted on a voluntary and optional basis."
steps.why: Auxiliary means helping or supporting. Regional languages help in their own regions. Spanish and Arabic are encouraged but are not official languages.

steps.action: The official languages are Filipino and English.

trapNotes.Filipino only: Filipino alone is the national language (Section 6). The official languages in Section 7 are Filipino and English.
trapNotes.Tagalog and English: The Constitution names the national language Filipino, not Tagalog. Section 7 lists Filipino and English.
trapNotes.Filipino, English and Spanish: Spanish is not an official language. Section 7 says Spanish and Arabic "shall be promoted on a voluntary and optional basis."
